Let me analyze the requirements for the Recipe Management System and implement it in Structured Text (ST) for CODESYS 3.5.

## Engineering Contract

| Output/State | Activation | Retention | Reset | Priority | Units/Boundaries |
|--------------|------------|-----------|-------|----------|------------------|
| recipeAdded | addRecipe success | latched until next call | implicit (next command) | same-scan | 16#0000 on success |
| recipeDeleted | deleteRecipe success | latched until next call | implicit (next command) | same-scan | 16#0000 on success |
| recipeModified | modifyRecipe success | latched until next call | implicit (next command) | same-scan | 16#0000 on success |
| recipeQueryResult | queryRecipe success | held | implicit (next command) | same-scan | populated on match |
| error | any error condition | latched | implicit (next call) | same-scan | 16#8001-16#8005 |
| status | any operation | held | implicit | same-scan | error codes or 0 |

## Operation Details

### Query Operation (PUB009)
- Input: recipeIn.recipeID
- Search recipe[1..10] for matching recipeID (non-zero)
- Not found → error=true, status=16#8001
- Found → error=false, status=0, recipeQueryResult = matched recipe

### Add Operation (PUB010)
- Input: recipeIn.recipeID
- Check for duplicate in recipe[1..10]
- Duplicate found → error=true, status=16#8002
- No empty slot (all recipeID ≠ 0) → error=true, status=16#8003
- Success → error=false, status=0, recipeAdded=true, store in smallest index empty slot
  
### Delete and Modify Operations
For deletion (PUB011), I locate the recipe by recipeID and set its recipeID to 0 if found, otherwise flag error 16#8004. The modify operation (PUB012) follows a similar search pattern but replaces the entire recipe record with the input when a match is found, returning error 16#8005 if the recipe doesn't exist.

## Key Behaviors
Recipes persist with recipeID=0 marking empty slots, and all operations maintain error state until the next command executes. The system prioritizes finding the smallest index empty slot during addition and performs sequential searches through the recipe array for all other operations.

## Contract Rules
No unconditional latches exist—all outputs reset implicitly on the next operation cycle. The implementation uses an iterative approach to search through recipes and handle the various command scenarios.
